Welcome · Start Here

Onboarding Overview

We are elated that you have officially joined our Husker Football Family. This portal walks you through every part of our onboarding process — by department, with the right contacts and forms in one place.

★ How This Works

What to Expect

There are many moving parts to onboarding. Throughout this process, staff from every department will be contacting you simultaneously seeking information — please be responsive to their calls, texts, and emails.

Use the tabs on the left to find what each department needs from you. The 8 departments have been organized for you, and each tab shows your contacts, action items, required forms, and step-by-step instructions.

overview

⚠ Reminder

Cleared to Move In ≠ Accepted

Student-athletes are NOT permitted to come to campus until cleared and approved prior to arrival. Recruiting will confirm your clearance status. Being accepted to UNL is a separate milestone — both are required.

Mental Health & Wellbeing

always available

Your mental health matters as much as your physical health. Whether you're managing the transition, homesick, struggling with pressure, or in crisis — these resources are here. Reaching out is a strength.

Team Resource →

Dr. Jacob Cooper

Sports Psychology · embedded with Nebraska Football. First point of contact for performance, anxiety, transition support. Confidential.
Campus Resource →

Big Red Resilience & Well-Being

UNL's resilience program — peer support, workshops, 1-on-1 coaching for stress, anxiety, sleep, and life transitions. Free for all students.
Campus Resource →

UNL CAPS

Counseling & Psychological Services — therapy, group counseling, psychiatry. Located in the University Health Center. Same-day urgent appointments available.
24/7 Crisis →

988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline

Call or text 988 any time, day or night. Free, confidential, 24/7 support for anyone in distress.
24/7 Crisis →

Crisis Text Line

Text HOME to 741741 to reach a trained crisis counselor any time. No phone call required.
Campus Resource →

UNL University Health Center

Comprehensive health services including primary care, mental health, pharmacy. Open weekdays · 24/7 nurse line for after-hours.

Frequently Asked

04 Q&A

When can I come to campus?

+

Student-athletes are NOT permitted to come to campus until they are cleared and approved prior to arrival. Recruiting will be in communication with you on whether you've been cleared to move in. Reminder: cleared to move in and being accepted are not the same thing.

Who are my roommates?

+

Your roommates will be other members of the football team. Thomas Bowling and Dr. Susan Elza are coordinating with University Housing on assignments. Roommate requests should be sent to Bowling or Elza as soon as possible.

Can I come back home for prom, graduation, and senior events?

+

Of course. We know being a senior in high school is important. As long as you communicate these dates with the head coach, position coach, and academic advisor, we'll always work with you to get you home for these special events.

Do parents/guardians need to attend orientation or stay after move-in?

+

Orientation is for the student-athlete only — parents are not required to attend. However, families are welcome to stay in the Lincoln area for as long as they would like.

    Insurance Policy

    read carefully
    ◆ The 30-Day Rule (Parents: This Is the Deadline)

    EOBs Must Be Submitted to Athletic Medicine Within 30 Days

    After your primary insurer processes a claim and sends an Explanation of Benefits (EOB), forward it — along with any remaining balance statements — to the Athletic Department within 30 days of receipt. Miss this window and Nebraska's secondary coverage may not pay. This is the single most important administrative deadline in this section.

    How payment works
    1. Your personal insurance is primary — it must be billed first for any athletically-related injury.
    2. Once your primary insurer responds (paid, partial, or denied), the Athletic Department's secondary/excess policy kicks in to cover the remainder.
    3. Submit the EOB + any balance statements to Athletic Medicine within 30 days. Nebraska handles the rest. Athletes and families do not pay out-of-pocket for athletically-related injuries.
    What's covered
    Injuries sustained during official, supervised football activities — practice, games, team workouts, team travel.
    Off-season & non-team activity
    Injuries during off-season conditioning or non-team activity are reviewed case-by-case. Always report new injuries to your athletic trainer immediately so the case can be opened and documented properly.
    Non-athletic medical care
    Sickness, dental, vision, mental health, prescriptions, and any non-football medical needs are the student-athlete's responsibility. Personal health insurance is strongly required — the UNL student plan is one option if family coverage isn't available.
    Who to contact
    Drew Hamblin, Head Football Athletic Trainer · 608.628.1947 · dhamblin@huskers.com
    Fax (for forms & EOBs)
    402.472.2006 — primary line for submitting insurance forms, EOBs, and physical claim documents to Athletic Medicine.

    10
    Your New City

    Living in Lincoln

    Lincoln is a college town of 300,000 with everything you need to settle in — getting around, where to grocery shop, where to eat off-campus, where to find what you need. Bookmark this tab; it's the one you'll come back to.

    ★ First Week Tip

    You Don't Need a Car

    Lincoln is built for students. UNL's StarTran bus system, BikeLNK rentals, and rideshare apps cover everything within a 15-minute reach of campus. Many freshmen live their entire first year without one.

    Getting Around

    transportation
    Free for students→

    RideLNK / StarTran Bus

    UNL students ride free with NCard. Routes connect City Campus, East Campus, downtown Lincoln, and major shopping. Live tracking via the StarTran app.
    Bike share→

    BikeLNK

    City-wide bike share — pick up at any docking station, drop at any other. Student rates available. Stations on both UNL campuses.
    Scooters→

    Bird / Lime Scooters

    E-scooter rentals via the Bird and Lime apps. Designated parking corrals across campus. Fastest way across City Campus when you're running late.
    Airport · LNK→

    Lincoln Airport (LNK)

    15 minutes from campus. Direct flights to Denver, Chicago, Dallas, Atlanta, and Minneapolis. Best when home is a connection through one of those hubs.
    Airport · OMA→

    Omaha Eppley Airfield (OMA)

    ~60 minutes from Lincoln. Larger airport, more direct flights to major cities. Use OMALink shuttle service to/from campus.
    Airport shuttle→

    OMALink Shuttle

    Reservation-based shuttle between Lincoln and Omaha airport. Multiple daily departures. Reserve online or via phone.
    Train→

    Amtrak · California Zephyr

    Lincoln Station serves the Chicago–San Francisco line. Student discount available. Platform is downtown, easy walk from campus.
    Rideshare→

    Uber & Lyft

    Both operate fully in Lincoln. Surge during games and weekend nights. Pick-up zones around campus and downtown clearly marked.

    Groceries

    stores in Lincoln

    From everyday staples to international ingredients, Lincoln has range. Most are 10–15 minutes from campus.

    Full grocery→

    Hy-Vee

    Multiple Lincoln locations. Iowa-based chain with deli, pharmacy, hot food bar. The closest go-to for most students.
    One-stop→

    Target

    Groceries plus dorm essentials, electronics, clothing. SuperTarget locations have a full grocery section.
    Budget→

    Walmart

    Multiple Lincoln Supercenters. Lowest grocery prices in town for staples.
    Budget→

    ALDI

    Discount grocery chain. Bring your own bags and a quarter for the cart. Surprisingly good produce and frozen items.
    Specialty→

    Trader Joe's

    South Lincoln location. Good for prepared foods, snacks, and unique items. Smaller and faster than a full grocery run.
    Bulk→

    Costco

    Membership warehouse. Worth it if you're cooking for roommates or buy household items in bulk.
    International→

    International Markets

    Lincoln has dedicated Asian, Latin, African, Halal, Indian, and Mediterranean grocers. Search "international market Lincoln NE" for a current map.
    Health food→

    Natural Grocers

    Organic, gluten-free, supplements. Good for specialty dietary needs.

    Eating Off-Campus

    food & coffee
    Campus dining→

    City & East Union Food Courts

    On-campus food courts at both unions accept Husker Bucks. Multiple national chains plus local options.
    Restaurants→

    Haymarket District

    Historic downtown area, walking distance from campus. Highest concentration of restaurants, breweries, coffee shops in Lincoln.
    Delivery→

    DoorDash

    Largest food delivery footprint in Lincoln. Most local restaurants are on it. DashPass available with student discount.
    Delivery→

    Uber Eats

    Strong Lincoln coverage. Often runs promos for students.
    Delivery→

    Grubhub

    Some Lincoln restaurants are exclusive to Grubhub. Worth installing all three apps.

    Pharmacy & Personal Care

    around campus
    Pharmacy→

    CVS

    Multiple Lincoln locations. 24-hour pharmacy at select stores. Accepts most insurance plans.
    Pharmacy→

    Walgreens

    Several Lincoln locations near campus. Photo printing, prescriptions, basics.
    On campus→

    UNL Health Center Pharmacy

    Located in the University Health Center. Files claims with most insurance plans, including the student plan.
    Vision→

    Eye Care & Vision

    Target Optical, LensCrafters, and several independent optometrists in Lincoln. Many take same-day appointments.

    Shopping

    malls & outlets
    Mall→

    Gateway Mall

    Largest enclosed mall in Lincoln. Macy's, Target, food court, movie theater. About 10 minutes from campus.
    Outdoor mall→

    SouthPointe Pavilions

    Open-air shopping center. Apple Store, Best Buy, Trader Joe's, restaurants, theater.
    Outlets→

    Nebraska Crossing Outlets

    30 minutes north toward Omaha. Nike, adidas, Lululemon, North Face, and 80+ outlet stores.
    Husker gear→

    Husker Team Store

    Official team merchandise. Located at Pinnacle Bank Arena. Online shop also available with student discounts.
    ◆ Pro Tip

    Get the Nebraska App First

    The official UNL mobile app combines bus routes, dining hours, campus maps, library tools, and emergency alerts in one place. Install it before move-in day. Link is on the Video & Tech tab.

    11
    UNL Campus Resources

    On-Campus Information

    Everything within UNL's borders — community resources for every kind of player, on-campus dining vendors, banking, books, the broader Nebraska Medicine network, and the offices that exist to support you outside of football.

    ★ Read This Tab

    UNL Has a Resource for Almost Anything You Need

    Beyond football, the university runs dedicated offices for international students, military and veteran students, multicultural support, religious community connections, and academic success. None of these cost extra. Find your people early.

    Community & Identity Resources

    find your people

    UNL operates dedicated support offices for many parts of the Husker community. Each is free to use and exists to help you succeed.

    International→

    International Student & Scholar Office (ISSO)

    Visa support, I-20 maintenance, work authorization, cultural transition resources. If you're an international player, ISSO is mandatory — meet with them in your first week alongside Jena Johnson.
    Multicultural→

    OASIS

    Office of Academic Success and Intercultural Services — multicultural student support, mentoring, scholarships, leadership programs, and community spaces.
    Inclusion→

    Jackie Gaughan Multicultural Center

    A home away from campus for all students: lounges and study spaces, student organizations, events, and community. Welcomes students of all backgrounds and identities.
    Military & Vet→

    Military & Veteran Success Center

    Support for student-athletes who are military service members, veterans, or military family members. Benefits navigation, community, advocacy.
    Global→

    Global Nebraska

    Cross-cultural community, conversation partner programs, global engagement events. Open to all students — domestic and international.
    Faith→

    Religious & Spiritual Communities

    Campus ministries and faith groups across traditions. Browse the member directory through ACReW, the Association of Campus Religious Workers.
    Wellbeing→

    Big Red Resilience & Well-Being

    Peer support, workshops, 1-on-1 coaching for stress, anxiety, sleep, and life transitions. Free for all students. Also linked from the Overview tab.

    Non-Football Medical Care

    campus health

    Athletic Medicine covers football injuries. Anything else — sickness, dental, prescriptions, mental health, routine care — runs through Nebraska Medicine on City Campus.

    ◆ Important for Families

    Many Services Are Already Covered

    Students who pay UNL's University Program and Facilities Fees (built into tuition) can receive certain services at the University Health Center at no extra charge. Bills are conveniently added to the student's consolidated UNL bill. Most insurance plans are also accepted.

    Primary care→

    University Health Center

    Walk-in, same-day, and appointment care for everything outside football injuries. Located on City Campus. Operated by Nebraska Medicine.
    Services→

    Service Directory

    Primary care, dental, vision, pharmacy, mental health, physical therapy, allergy & immunization, sexual & reproductive health, specialty referrals.
    Pharmacy→

    On-Campus Pharmacy

    Inside the University Health Center. Files claims with most insurance plans. Convenient for prescriptions while you're on campus.
    Mental health→

    Counseling & Psychological Services (CAPS)

    Therapy, group counseling, psychiatry, same-day urgent appointments. Located inside the University Health Center.

    Banking on Campus

    accounts & ATMs
    ◆ For International Players

    Union Bank Has a Branch Inside the City Union

    Many international student-athletes choose Union Bank specifically because of its on-campus location and the network of ATMs across UNL and downtown Lincoln. Open a checking or savings account in person without leaving campus. Most major Lincoln banks are also within walking distance of campus.

    On-campus branch→

    Union Bank & Trust

    Branch located inside City Union. ATMs on both UNL campuses and downtown. Recommended starting point — especially for international students.
    Off-campus→

    First Nebraska Bank

    Multiple Lincoln branches close to campus. Local Nebraska bank with strong student account options.
    National→

    U.S. Bank, Wells Fargo, Pinnacle Bank

    National and regional banks with multiple Lincoln locations. If you already have an account, find the closest branch through the bank's site.

    On-Campus Dining

    student unions

    When you're not at Training Table, the two student unions cover the rest. Husker Bucks and NCard accepted at most vendors. Both unions are walking distance from class.

    City Campus→

    Nebraska Union (City Campus)

    Vendors: Starbucks · Imperial Place · Subway · Valentino's · Chick-fil-A · Steak 'n Shake. Plus market and grab-and-go options.
    East Campus→

    East Union (East Campus)

    Vendors: Starbucks · East Campus Dining Center. Smaller footprint, less crowded — favored by students based out east.
    All locations→

    UNL Dining Services

    Full directory of every dining hall, cafe, market, and food court on campus. Hours, menus, and meal plan info.
    Husker classic→

    UNL Dairy Store

    Operated by the Department of Food Science & Technology. Ice cream and cheese made on-campus. East Campus location. Worth the trip.
    Husker classic→

    Loeffel Meat Shoppe

    Department of Animal Science storefront. Beef, pork, lamb, sausage, and bratwurst — processed on-campus. East Campus.

    International Grocery in Lincoln

    by cuisine

    Lincoln has a deep international grocery scene. If you're missing flavors from home, one of these will have what you need. Most are 10–20 minutes from campus.

    African
    African Home Food Supply
    Asian
    Asian City Mart · Dai Phat Market · KT Market · Little Saigon Asian Grocery · Hong Kong Market · Jung's Oriental Food Store · Oriental Market · Viet Hao Market
    European
    Harvest European Market · European Grocery Deli
    Halal
    Al Mustafa Market · Alfourat Grocery · Global Foods of Lincoln · Teeba Market
    Hispanic / Latin
    Guerrero Grocery · Lobo's City Mex Supermarket · Marlene's Tortilleria
    Indian
    Suji's Indian Grocery
    Mediterranean
    Lincoln Mediterranean Market
    Specialty
    El Mercato (certified beef)

    Need directions? Search the store name in the Nebraska App or any maps app — most have full addresses listed online.

    Books & Textbooks

    save money

    Don't pay full retail. Most textbooks can be rented or bought used at a significant discount. The University Bookstore price-matches if you find the same book cheaper online.

    On campus→

    University Bookstore

    Locations in both the City Union and East Union. Rent or buy textbooks. Price-matches against Amazon and other online retailers — bring proof.
    Online→

    UNL Online Textbooks

    Order textbooks online through UNL's official portal. Pickup on campus or shipping to your address.
    Rentals→

    Amazon Textbooks

    Often the cheapest option for rentals. Buy or rent. Free Prime Student trial gives free shipping. Bring price quote to University Bookstore for match.
    Used→

    eBay

    Used textbooks at deep discount, especially for older editions still in use. Check ISBN matches before buying.
    Free→

    UNL Libraries

    Many course textbooks are on reserve at the library — free to check out. Digital options also available. Always check before buying.
